newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Thousands march for third day in Albanian port.
newsitem.headline: Thousands march for third day in Albanian port.

text.p: At least 15,000 protesters poured through this Albanian port for the third consecutive day on Friday demanding the resignation of the rightist government and refunds of money trapped in failed investment schemes.

"Give us back our money!" the crowd shouted as it surged towards regional administration offices. Police ringed the building but took no action. "Vlore police, take off your uniforms, join us!" cried the marchers.

The marchers later made for Independence Square, where they have massed for the past two days. The gatherings denounce President Sali Berisha but appear spontaneous, with no leaders heading columns and neither government nor opposition politicians present.

Two young boys on horseback had led the procession down the city's main palm-lined boulevard. The marchers paused twice in front of a high school and technical college to persuade students to leave their classrooms and go into the street.
Police had tried unsuccessfully on Wednesday to break up the demonstration but have since allowed angry investors to proceed unimpeded through city streets.

The protests, so far confined to Vlore, are the first since a wave of violence swept through Albanian towns last month in response to the collapse of five of the schemes promising quick, lucrative returns. Authorities cracked down by arresting more than 150 people and threatening them with long jail terms.
